vatican-city.title: Flag of Vatican City

use.as: national flag and state flag of the Holy See

colors.note: Represents the golden key of Heaven in the Papal emblem.
Represents the silver key of Earth and the papacy.
The papal tiara and gold key depict spiritual authority.
The cord binding the keys — a detail from the Holy See emblem.

desc:
- Two equal vertical bands of yellow (hoist) and white (fly), with the papal emblem centred on the white
- The emblem consists of the triregnum (three-tiered papal tiara) and two crossed keys — one gold, one silver, bound with a red cord
- Adopted on 7 June 1929 when the Vatican City State was established by the Lateran Treaty with Italy
trivia:
- Along with Switzerland's, Vatican City's flag is one of only two national flags with a square ratio (1:1)
- The crossed keys represent the 'keys of the kingdom of heaven' given by Christ to Saint Peter in the Gospel of Matthew
- The Holy See holds permanent observer status at the United Nations rather than full membership
